AbstractIn the current era of technological development, medical imaging plays an important part in several applications of medical diagnosis and therapy. This requires more precise images with much more details and information for correct medical diagnosis and therapy. Medical image fusion is one of the solutions for obtaining much spatial and spectral information in a single image. This article presents an optimization‐based contourlet image fusion approach in addition to a comparative study for the performance of both multi‐resolution and multi‐scale geometric effects on fusion quality. An optimized multi‐scale fusion technique based on the Non‐Subsampled Contourlet Transform (NSCT) using the Modified Central Force Optimization (MCFO) and local contrast enhancement techniques is presented. The first step in the proposed fusion approach is the histogram matching of one of the images to the other to allow the same dynamic range for both images. The NSCT is used after that to decompose the images to be fused into their coefficients. The MCFO technique is used to determine the optimum decomposition level and the optimum gain parameters for the best fusion of coefficients based on certain constraints. Finally, an additional contrast enhancement process is applied on the fused image to enhance its visual quality and reinforce details. The proposed fusion framework is subjectively and objectively evaluated with different fusion quality metrics including average gradient, local contrast, standard deviation (STD), edge intensity, entropy, peak signal‐to‐noise ratio, Q
ab/f, and processing time. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed optimized NSCT medical image fusion approach based on the MCFO and histogram matching achieves a superior performance with higher image quality, average gradient, edge intensity, STD, better local contrast and entropy, a good quality factor, and much more details in images. These characteristics help for more accurate medical diagnosis in different medical applications.

result.paraphrase: Abstract This article examines the role of medical imaging in diagnosis and therapy and the need for more detailed, precise images to support accurate clinical decisions. It proposes an optimization-based contourlet image fusion method and compares multi-resolution and multi-scale geometric effects on fusion quality. The framework uses an optimized multi-scale fusion technique based on the Non-Subsampled Contourlet Transform (NSCT), the Modified Central Force Optimization (MCFO), and local contrast enhancement. First, one image is histogram-matched to the other so both share the same dynamic range. The images are then decomposed into NSCT coefficients. MCFO is applied to find the optimal decomposition level and gain parameters under specified constraints for coefficient fusion. Lastly, an extra contrast-enhancement step is performed on the fused image to improve visual quality and highlight details. The method is evaluated subjectively and objectively using average gradient, local contrast, standard deviation (STD), edge intensity, entropy, peak signal-to-noise ratio, Qab/f, and processing time. Experiments show that the optimized NSCT medical image fusion approach with MCFO and histogram matching yields superior performance, with higher image quality, stronger average gradient, edge intensity, and STD, improved local contrast and entropy, a good quality factor, and more image detail, supporting more accurate medical diagnosis in various medical applications.
